model: Entry tier, T4300 / TU7000 / AU7000 class
userAgent: Mozilla/5.0 (SMART-TV; LINUX; Tizen 5.5) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) 69.0.3497.106.1/5.5 TV Safari/537.36
cpuApproximation: Estimated TV proxy: half Chrome DevTools' measured low tier mobile BenchmarkIndex of 264. The extra 2x margin allows for older TV clocks and engine behavior. It is not a measured Samsung score. Calibrate the current laptop to this workload rather than using a fixed slowdown.
why: A conservative development approximation of an entry Samsung TV from 2020. Published hardware facts, project stress limits and estimated CPU speed are identified separately. Passing it is useful evidence, not certification of every TV.

sources.cores and memory: Samsung's Common Criteria Security Targets state the minimum hardware for each Tizen version. For Tizen 5.5 (2020) and 6.0 (2021): quad Cortex-A53, 1.0GB DDR, 4GB eMMC. Samsung publishes no RAM or CPU figures anywhere in the developer documentation, calling them confidential, so this is the only first party source there is.
sources.which models: The 20TV_BASIC1 and 20TV_BASIC2 groups in Samsung's TV Model Groups table. BASIC2 is the floor of the floor: it is the one 2020 group absent from Samsung's multitasking support list, Samsung excludes it from Tap View, and other app vendors decline to support it outright. Still sold new as a current model into 2024 and receiving firmware, so it is a live target rather than a museum piece.
sources.engine: Samsung's Web Engine Specifications: Tizen 5.5 is Chromium 69, Tizen 6.0 is Chromium 76. Sets from 2020 to 2022 never receive an engine upgrade, only 2023 and later do, so these stay where they are.
sources.heap: 120MB is a conservative project V8 old space stress cap. It is not a measured TV JavaScript heap limit, an emulation of 1GB physical RAM or a cap on the browser's total native and GPU allocations.
sources.speed: Chrome DevTools calibrates to a low tier mobile Lighthouse BenchmarkIndex of 264. The proxy target here is 132, a further 2x engineering margin for older TV hardware and browser behavior. This margin is estimated, not measured on a Samsung TV. The current host is calibrated to this score at every run and checked again afterwards. Source: https://developer.chrome.com/blog/devtools-grounded-real-world

caveats: The engine cannot be downgraded. The user agent says Chromium 69 and the resources match an entry set, but the code still runs on whatever Chrome is installed, so a feature missing in 69 will work here and fail there. The build already targets es2019 for that reason; CSS has no equivalent and has to be checked by hand.
The panel on these models is often 1366x768, but the application resolution is 1920x1080 on every Samsung TV regardless, so the viewport is unchanged.
Video on this tier is capped at FHD, and MSE does not do UHD at all.

CPU throttling suspends the renderer main thread, affecting JavaScript, style and layout. Worker threads, raster, compositing, image decoding and the GPU are not constrained to TV speeds. Frame cadence is a main thread estimate, not a measurement of TV GPU or video frames.

A matching workload score does not reproduce CPU architecture, memory bandwidth, flash latency or the old browser engine. A real TV measurement is the way to replace the proxy estimate with evidence. Benchmark playback uses a clock and state shim so hls.js does not add CPU work that native AVPlay would not perform.
